transport: Offline authoring via direct HTTPS POST https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/audio/speech. No runtime speech API.
format: mono 48000 Hz Opus, 96 kbps VBR; source: mono 24000 Hz signed 16-bit PCM
processing: Owner-approved voice-plus-grit parallel treatment. Wide-band clean body plus driven band-limited branch, then active-RMS matching; no pitch shifts, fake gunfire or baked reverb.

rights.source: Original text and official prebuilt synthetic voices; no uploaded reference audio, voice cloning, performer or celebrity impersonation.
rights.basis: Google Gemini API terms state Google will not claim ownership over generated original content. OpenRouter defers output rights to model terms. This is not a guarantee of exclusivity, copyright or third-party clearance.
rights.review: Owner selected this focused generated bank for game integration. Applicable provider terms govern use and redistribution; no rights to provider voice models or original library reactions are conveyed.

reactionIdentity: Speech cast uses actor ID modulo four; existing nonverbal groups use the same ID modulo two. Each speech identity has a fixed reaction group, not a claimed same-performer match. In-game compatibility remains an owner listening check.

orus-spot-1.instructions: You're moving cautiously with a teammate when you suddenly catch sight of an enemy aiming at you. You have a split second to alert your teammate as you pull back into cover. The word comes out as a sharp, instinctive warning, your breath tightening at the sudden danger. Voice only, without background sound effects.

orus-reload-1.instructions: You've ducked behind cover with an empty magazine while your teammate keeps firing. As you change magazines, you give them a quick heads-up that you can't cover them yet. You're slightly winded and concentrating on the reload; the words are practical and almost incidental, just loud enough for the teammate nearby. Voice only, without background sound effects.

orus-grenade-1.instructions: You're crouched behind cover in a firefight. Your teammate is covering you while you throw a grenade toward the enemy. As it leaves your hand, you give your teammate a quick heads-up. You're tense and slightly winded; the words are pushed out naturally between breaths, loud enough to carry over the fighting, not a deliberate announcement. Voice only, without background sound effects.
